arxiv-1806-04345.title: Homological mirror symmetry for Milnor fibers via moduli of A ∞ A_{\infty} -structures
arxiv-1806-04345.creator: Yankı Lekili, Kazushi Ueda
arxiv-1806-04345.description: Abstract . We show that the base spaces of the semiuniversal unfoldings of some weighted homogeneous singularities can be identified with moduli spaces of A ∞ A_{\infty} -structures on the trivial extension algebras of the endomorphism algebras of the tilting objects. The same algebras also appear in the Fukaya categories of their mirrors.

arxiv-2107-11315.title: Norms of inclusions between some spaces of analytic functions
arxiv-2107-11315.creator: Adrián Llinares
arxiv-2107-11315.description: Abstract . The inclusions between the Besov spaces B q B^{q} , the Bloch space ℬ \mathcal{B} and the standard weighted Bergman spaces A α p A^{p}_{\alpha} are completely understood, but the norms of the corresponding inclusion operators are in general unknown. In this work, we compute or estimate asymptotically the norms of these inclusions.

pmc-11499301.title: Using Empirical Performance Data to Source Bluebunch and Snake River Wheatgrass Plant Materials to Restoration Sites in the Eastern Great Basin, USA
pmc-11499301.creator: Thomas A Jones, Thomas A Monaco
pmc-11499301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To infer adaptation of plant material, restoration practitioners often consider only surrogate geographic or climatic information. However, empirical biomass data could assist in deciding what material to use where. To test this approach, we transplanted seven bluebunch wheatgrass (BBWG; Pseudoroegneria spicata) and five Snake River wheatgrass (SRWG; Elymus wawawaiensis) populations to three sites ranging from low to high precipitation (LPPT, MPPT, and HPPT). We measured establishment‐year (2011) biomass at all sites and 2012–16 biomass at MPPT and HPPT.

pmc-11520683.title: First report of Angiostrongylus vasorum in an African golden wolf (Canis lupaster) in Algeria
pmc-11520683.creator: Noureddine Mechouck, Georgiana Deak, Angela Monica Ionică, Corina Toma, Andrada Gabriela Negoescu, Marian Taulescu, Zihad Bouslama, Andrei Daniel Mihalca
pmc-11520683.description: BackgroundAngiostrongylus vasorum, commonly known as the “French heartworm,” is a nematode belonging to the Metastrongyloidea superfamily. This parasite was first identified in Toulouse, France in 1853 infecting the pulmonary arteries and the right side of the heart of a Pointer dog.

pmc-11603674.creator: Belay Desye, Amensisa Hailu Tesfaye, Chala Daba, Embay Amare Alemseged, Yonas Angaw, Ahmed Mohammed Ebrahim, Tarikuwa Natnael, Seada Hassen, Lebasie Woretaw
pmc-11603674.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe increasing use of pesticides has become a global public health concern. The problem is more devastating in developing countries, which deters the implementation of effective intervention strategies. Moreover, the existing evidences are inconsistent and not comprehensive.

pmc-11677075.title: Effect of Hot Water Bottle and Cloth Blanket on Rectal Temperature During Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Head in Cats Under General Anesthesia
pmc-11677075.creator: Ruxandra Pavel, Cristina Fernoagă, Alexandru Gabriel Neagu, Ruxandra Costea, Carmen Solcan, Gheorghe Solcan
pmc-11677075.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Maintaining an animal’s body temperature during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) poses great challenges, as many temperature measuring devices and warming systems are incompatible with the MRI machine. The aim of this study was to examine body temperature changes and evaluate the impact of using a hot water bottle and a cloth blanket on rectal temperature during magnetic resonance imaging in cats.

pmc-13124519.title: Association between fluid balance trajectories and prognosis in older patients with malnutrition: a group-based trajectory model analysis
pmc-13124519.creator: Chunmei Zhang, Zhiyi Xie, Qitian Zhang, Xiaohong Huang
pmc-13124519.description: BackgroundFluid balance plays a crucial role in the management of older patients with malnutrition; however, the impact of different fluid balance trajectories on prognosis has not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the association between fluid balance trajectories and the risk of 30-day mortality in older patients with malnutrition.

pmc-13336217.title: Semantic congruence impacts audiovisual processing in the Colavita effect
pmc-13336217.creator: Keira Dyck, Abigail Mitchell, Jonathan Wilbiks, Geneviève Desmarais, Elisa Scerrati, Elisa Scerrati, Elisa Scerrati, Elisa Scerrati, Elisa Scerrati
pmc-13336217.description: The Colavita effect is a phenomenon that occurs when participants are presented with auditory, visual, and audiovisual stimuli and are tasked to identify the modality of the stimuli. When audiovisual stimuli are presented, participants occasionally miss the auditory component and report that the stimulus was visual only – reflecting visual dominance.

pmc-13406853.title: Nutritional Follow-Up in Indigenous Children Under Five Years in Colombia
pmc-13406853.creator: Pedro Barrera-López, Andrés Felipe Mora-Salamanca, Kevin Rico, Sandra Barrera-Ayala
pmc-13406853.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Nutritional alterations were highly prevalent among Wayúu children under five years of age in Manaure, with chronic malnutrition and stunting being the dominant pattern, whereas acute malnutrition was comparatively infrequent.In the exploratory longitudinal follow-up subgroup, descriptive analysis of anthropometric indicators suggested possible patterns of growth impairment over time, particularly in weight-for-age and height-for-age indicators.

pmc-13494995.title: Evaluation of host-immune biomarker signatures as multiplex qPCR diagnostic assays: a pilot study toward meeting WHO target product profiles for TB diagnosis in India
pmc-13494995.creator: Harriet N. Garlant, Kalaiarasan Ellappan, Noyal Mariya Joseph, Carrie Turner, Vishnukanth Govindaraj, Saka Vinod Kumar, Sanjeev Kumar, Seshadri Vasan, Karen E. Kempsell
pmc-13494995.description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Current diagnostic tools are limited, especially in low-resource settings. The World Health Organization's (WHO) Target Product Profiles (TPPs) call for rapid, non-sputum-based diagnostics with high sensitivity and specificity.

pmc-13594736.title: Tumor genomic landscape of older patients with metastatic breast cancer☆
pmc-13594736.creator: H. Gupta, K.D. Brantley, T. Grinda, R.A. Freedman, A. Kodali, G.J. Kirkner, M.E. Hughes, A. Higgins, A.B. Newman, S. Avdulla, J. Files, G. Suggs, S.M. Tolaney, D. Dillon, L. Sholl, A.C. Garrido-Castro, A.D. Cherniack, N.U. Lin
pmc-13594736.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMetastatic breast cancer (MBC) in older patients has distinct clinical and histologic characteristics. Elucidating the genomic basis of MBC helps identify potential therapeutic targets to improve outcomes for older patients with MBC.Patients and methodsUsing a prospective database and targeted DNA sequencing (OncoPanel), we examined MBC’s genomic landscape in older patients (age ≥70 years at MBC diagnosis) and compared findings with those in younger (aged <50 years) and middle-aged (aged 50-69 years) patients.
